lesson.subtitle: Lesson 1 -- The Second Sentence
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Andreia Naim Finianos | Lesson 1 -- The Second Sentence

listenings.text: People ask me what I sell and I always want to say software, because that is the easy answer, but it is not really true. What I sell is the answer to a question somebody could not answer last year. I had a client, a group with about four thousand people, and their headcount had doubled in eighteen months, and they had opened in two more countries, and the old system kept working the whole time. That was the problem. It kept working. Nobody noticed that the numbers had stopped being right until an auditor asked for one report and the whole thing came apart. So the one thing I have learned to do, and it took me years, is to ask what went wrong last year before I show anybody anything. The pain point is never on the list they send you. It is the thing nobody wants to put in writing.

We looked at four providers and honestly the demos were all the same. The one we chose was not the cheapest and their demo was not even the best one. They were the only ones who asked us what had gone wrong the year before, and I remember thinking, well, at least these people are paying attention. Now, we made one mistake and it was ours, not theirs. We went live on a Friday, at the end of the month, which is the worst possible combination, and of course the first payroll run failed and there was nobody in the building. What saved that weekend was a person on their side who called me on Saturday morning and walked my team through it screen by screen, for two days, on the phone. I still have his number in my phone. I would move providers before I would give up that number.
